title: Representative normalization of conjugated coefficient tensor maps
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, an arbitrary scheme $W$, and a coefficient fiber calculus $S$ [def-coef-derived-system-calculus-data]. For the explicit normalized reduction data and quotient data of [def-pur-canonical-coefficient-reduction], all five representative normalization equations hold: simultaneous strict reduction tensor normalization, finite scalar tensor normalization, sequence evaluation tensor normalization, reduction tensor evaluation, and finite quotient tensor normalization. The strict complexes, quotient identifications, representative maps and their pure-tensor formulas are exactly those of $S$. No enriched, fiber-Hom composition, or global-sections existence is asserted.

proof.text: The new integral, sequence and finite tensor-model isomorphisms are definitionally the old ones followed by the adjoint comparisons. Reuse the old strict complexes, augmentations and representative maps. Apply tensorSquare to the old simultaneous reduction, finite scalar, evaluation and quotient squares. It cancels the source comparison and moves the target comparison by naturality, proving all four representative normalizations.

proof.text: Apply evaluation_transport to the old reductionTensor_evaluation equation. The sequence comparison cancels with its inverse, and naturality of the finite comparison and reductionEvaluation give precisely the new equation. Package the five proved equations as RepresentativeLaws.
